# @tilia/query

Offline-first reactive query engine for Tilia, connected to a store factory.
The shipped Store is a write-through cache with optimistic writes, ordered
outbox, query registry, rejection records, and local retention.

## Authority

If prose differs, follow:

- TypeScript root API: `src/index.d.ts`
- ReScript root API: `src/TiliaQuery.resi`
- TypeScript IndexedDB API: `src/indexeddb.d.ts`
- npm exports: `package.json`

Installed package contracts:

- `@tilia/query` types: `dist/index.d.ts`
- `@tilia/query/indexeddb` types: `dist/indexeddb.d.ts`
- ReScript: `src/TiliaQuery.resi`

Package exports only `.`, `./indexeddb`, and `./package.json`.

## Default construction

```ts
import { Store, make } from "@tilia/query";
import { make as indexedDb } from "@tilia/query/indexeddb";

const [query, store] = make<T, Q, Store<T>>({
  id,
  matches,
  store: Store.make<T, Q>({
    find(query, answer) {},       // answer.fresh(values) | answer.fail(message)
    upsert(value, reply) {},      // saved | conflict | rejected | transient
    remove(id, reply) {},         // removed | rejected | transient
    persist: indexedDb({name: "app"}),
    merge,
    expiry: {local: 2_592_000_000},
  }),
  expiry: {refresh: 30_000, memory: 300_000},
  onError(query, message) {},
});
```

`make({id, matches, store, expiry?, now?, key?, sort?, onError?})` returns
`[TiliaQuery<T,Q>, S]`, where `S` is what the store factory offers. With the
shipped store, `S` is `Store<T>`.

Engine defaults: refresh 30 s, memory 5 min, `Date.now`,
`sortedStringify(query)`, identity sort.

Store defaults: shared `Store.online()`, `Store.memory()` Kv, local expiry
30 days.

Queries and shipped-store values are plain JSON data. `matches(query,value)`
is a pure per-row predicate; finds return full result sets. No pagination,
limits, or aggregates. Backend confirmations preserve client ids.

## Reads

`query.one(q)` and `query.array(q)` return:

```ts
"loading"
| {state: "loaded"; claim: "partial" | "local" | "fresh"; data: T}
| {state: "noData"; reason:
    "offline"
    | {reason: "failed"; message: string}
    | {reason: "noMatch"; claim: Claim}}
```

Claim order is `partial < local < fresh`. Weaker answers never replace
stronger answers. Only `tick()` weakens `fresh` to `local`.

- non-empty partial = renderable data
- empty partial online = loading
- empty partial offline = noData/offline
- complete empty array = loaded `[]`
- only `one` maps complete empty to noData/noMatch with its claim
- failure with no data = noData/failed
- failure with visible data = keep data and call engine `onError`

`tick()` drives refresh, aging, memory eviction, store retry, and local purge.
Call at least twice per refresh interval. `dispose()` closes finds, runs
teardowns, stops watches, then disposes the store.

## Shipped Store

Application API:

```ts
store.upsert(value)
store.remove(id)
store.receive.changed(values)
store.receive.removed(ids)
store.status.pending
store.status.rejected
store.retry(rejection)
store.discard(rejection)
```

Writes update memory/query membership/persistence immediately and enqueue an
ordered op. Persisted ops replay at boot and reconnect.

`Store.make` sends one op at a time in outbox order:

- upsert `{outcome:"saved", value}` confirms
- remove `"removed"` confirms
- `{outcome:"conflict", value}` rebases through `merge`; successful merge
  stays pending for the next tick, declined merge records conflict
- `{outcome:"rejected", message}` rejects only that op and continues
- `"transient"` stops; current and later ops stay pending

`merge(change, remote)` mutates the local object in place and returns boolean.
Change tags: clean `{value}`, created `{edited}`, updated `{base,edited}`,
removed `{base}`.

Rejection tags: createConflict, createFailed, updateConflict, updateFailed,
removeConflict, removeFailed. They are deep JSON snapshots, not persisted ops
or overlays. Remote/base truth is already visible. `status.rejected` is in
outbox order regardless of reply order, at most one per id; a write to the id
clears it. `retry`/`discard` act only on the exact current record. Retry
reapplies a copy through the normal optimistic path against current truth.

## Persistence

`Kv` is one string keyspace:

```ts
get(tag, keys | undefined, set)
keys(tag, set)
set(tag, key, value | undefined)
```

The shipped store keeps rows (`Store.rowTag === "row"`), query records, and
outbox entries under tags in that keyspace. Query records contain key, query,
ids, and lastSeen. Pending ops and surviving records root rows during
mark-and-sweep purge. Purge first runs on the first tick, then at most every
`local / 8`.

`@tilia/query/indexeddb` exports only `make({name, store?, version?,
onError?}): Kv`. It uses one object store with compound key `[tag,key]`,
batches writes, and flushes writes before reads. Persistence errors are
reported to its own `onError`; failed reads answer empty and writes drop.

## Advanced custom channels

Use `Store.custom({remote, persist?, lookup?, merge?, expiry?})` for a
channel-backed remote, especially live/server-push sources.

Remote read channel:

- `fresh(values)`: complete authoritative snapshot
- `live(values)`: same, source owns freshness; engine skips refresh
- `fail(message)`: report without closing
- `end()`: close and return live query to periodic refresh
- `finally(fn)`: one teardown slot, run once on close

Remote write channel:

- `set(value)`, `removed(id)`: confirm one op
- `conflict(value)`: answer one op; an accepted merge keeps it pending,
  while a declined or missing merge records a conflict and clears it
- `reject(id,message)`: reject one op
- `retry()`: terminal; unanswered ops stay pending
- `fail(message)`: terminal; reject all unanswered ops

First terminal call wins; closed-channel callbacks are noops. Going offline
does not end a live find. `receive.changed/removed` are inbound facts and do
not affect query freshness.

`lookup(query,{partial,local})` may claim local only if its own index proves a
complete answer.
